page.layout: One printed page. Running verse in the main column with a heading in capitals and a verse block below it. A fragment of verse runs at the top, then a heading "SITTACO, SPECIE QVADAM MOERORIS, Domino aegrotante, mortuo." followed by verse. Page number 73 at top right. Small marks in the margins are not text.

main_text.p: Et vos, Aesculapi soboles dignissima, Vestro
Iam vir Paeonia celeberrimus arte, chorique
Hic vos flete simul patres, quos cura tenella
Iam terras hic dena pater post lustra relinquens
Aeque tuum decet, o Saracenum flere, Geneua,
main_text.head: SITTACO, SPECIE QVADAM MOERORIS, Domino aegrotante, mortuo.
main_text.p: Sittacus Eois quo nullus missus ab oris,
Quo nullus, Vel amabilius, Vel suauius, omnes
Languentem miseratus herum mox languit ipse:
main_text.l: Et fuit (o fatum!) tam grauis ille dolor,
main_text.p: Ut pia maluerit Vitam finire Volucris,
main_text.l: Tot mala quam Domini tam diuturna pati:
main_text.p: Aut, an ex hominum infidis nunc caetibus, exul

l.i: Ad genus hoc Volucrum fugit amicitia?

page.notes: Verse lines are partly illegible at the left edge; the transcription of the first lines and of the text at the edges is uncertain. Some letters in the Greek-influenced words are doubtful, and the first line is cut off by the page edge.
